# nova-sprint roadmap

<!-- Generated from docs/roadmap.sexp by tools/roadmap. Do not edit this file: edit docs/roadmap.sexp and run `make roadmap`. -->

This is the nova-sprint, nova-card and nova-work work after the point releases. The release plan (the owner, 2026-10-11) replaces the ladder of 2026-10-09. The v1.2.x point releases come first and are cut in turn: v1.2.10 (being cut), v1.2.11 small fixes, v1.2.12 tests and models only, v1.2.13 contraction (fewer lines, no behaviour change), v1.2.14 the next small fixes; FIXES.md holds each one's scope and fixes, and an item below whose target is a v1.2.x release is waiting for its card. The aim is v1.2.x working pretty well, so it is the reference for intended behaviour: v1.3, unstable, is the re-architecture (the client/server conversion, then each layer secured from the bottom), built by the sprint running on v1.2.x and checked against it, rather than a blind rewrite; like getting a compiler self-hosting, then using it to build a better compiler. v1.4 is the stable release of v1.3, architecturally correct top to bottom. Every item's :release is one of four values (the owner, 2026-10-12): v1.2.x (a point release, named in the item's text), v1.3, v1.4 (stabilization: tests, models and cleanups, no features) or later (a list, not a release); the roadmap tool refuses any other. The v1.3 work is grouped by theme below, in build order, behind the v1.3 test plan that every v1.3 entry lands after; each v1.3 item ends with the behaviour that proves it done (Done when), measurable on the bench, and names the items it absorbed in the de-duplication of 2026-10-12. Point releases continue until only architectural items are open: an area stops taking point fixes when a fix there is the same problem in another form, or would be its third, and each v1.3 architectural item names the point fixes it replaces. Friend work is dogfooded within the week, once more friends are online: friends alone, then friends and fleet together, each friend bug a point-release card. These items were the sprint half of nova-tools' roadmap and moved here with the split, with the sprint's docs and models; nova-tools' ROADMAP.md holds the rest. Point-release work is in FIXES.md, not here. Each item says what it is and why it waits. Where the code already has part of an item, the item says what exists and covers only the gap.

## v1.3: the test plan comes first

The plan every v1.3 entry lands behind: the test tiers, the bench hosts per tier and the pass bar. Nothing in v1.3 lands before it (the owner, 2026-10-12). The document lives in nova-tools.

### The v1.3 test plan

The mirror of nova-tools' entry of the same id: the plan, docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md in nova-tools, is written before any v1.3 code. The tiers every theme ships with: unit (twin or fake store, parallel, under a minute); functional (real Redis and Postgres, one test per Lua function); integration (seat, member and friend together on a bench); stress and load (deals of 3,000 cards, a 140-width fleet, 200 reads, the bus at 10 messages a second); TLA+ (a model with reversed witnesses, TLC on a bench); release checks (the parallel functional suite under two minutes). The Linux benches hetzner2, space and vision run the functional, integration, stress and TLC tiers; the studio never runs a tier. Green before and after each change, the measured numbers recorded. No v1.3 card lands without its tier's tests; every v1.3 entry below lands only after this one. Done when: nova-tools docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md is committed naming every tier, bench host and load number, and nova-sprint add refuses a v1.3 card whose brief names no tier of it.

Why it waits: The owner, 2026-10-12: the plan is created before a line of v1.3 code is written.

### Friends table reads presence owned by nova-tools

The sprint consumes friend presence from the friend tool instead of owning it, so the friends table stays right while the sprint server is stopped or hung. Absorbs (de-duplicated 2026-10-12): A batch friend's presence is her engine's beat (batch-friend-presence-from-engine-beat); Supervised wake adapters for coordinator seats (coordinator-push-wake-adapters). The sprint reads presence from the comms module (the-comms-module-holds-presence-capability-and-timers, nova-tools roadmap) and the wake capability from nova-wake's record; the nova-tools items friend-presence-from-the-session and friend-daemon-liveness retire with the old comms paths. The states are the owner's three, working (with a blocked flag), asleep and down, plus the freshness fields the record carries: session generation, sequence, age, expiry and reach; an expired proof reads unknown, never an inferred down (docs/SPEC-COMMS.md 3.2 and 6.2, nova-tools; friend-down-detection says what turns unknown into down). Its tests are comms-test-plan. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: the friends table shows working, working blocked, asleep, down and unknown with sgen, seq, age, expiry and reach from the comms presence record alone, with no beat loop of the sprint's own and no field named alive, up or live, a planted expired proof reading unknown and never down, pinned by a functional test on a real Redis and a class test on the column names.

Target: v1.3

From: card moved out of the sprint (work record, 2026-10-04)

### Detect a friend AI that is unreachable or out of credits and route around it

A friend counts as down when she cannot work: her session said so (a provider refusal, a limit, an empty balance, said once with its cause and end) or a judgment said so. Down is a word written, never inferred: a lapsed presence proof is a stale proof, not absence (docs/SPEC-COMMS.md 3.2, in nova-tools), and the sweep (nova-wake check, every DetectEvery, 10 min) marks it reach unknown, which the friends table shows as unknown with the proof's age. What turns unknown into down is a judgment with its evidence: the tick raises one to the seat when a friend's reach has read unknown for UnknownRaisesAfter (a setting, default 2 x PresenceTTL = 20 min, proposed), and the seat's answer (down with cause and end, or hold) is the word the table shows. Her work is routed around her once the word is down. Absorbs (de-duplicated 2026-10-12): A held or down friend returns its cards to ready (held-friend-returns-dealt-and-started-cards); A broken session or a limit means down (friend-broken-session-and-limits-mean-down, nova-tools roadmap); Friends and machines noticed back up and made current (friend-back-up-detection-and-adopt, nova-tools roadmap); A broken friend session renews itself (friend-session-auto-recovery, nova-tools roadmap). A refusal, a limit or an empty balance is said once by the session and reads down; a hold or down carries its cause and end; a returning friend (a fresh report with a newer session generation) adopts first (the adopt half is adoption-pipeline-automated, nova-tools roadmap); a down friend's dealt and started cards bounce back to ready at the tick; a partner who goes down is pushed to the other. Its tests are comms-test-plan. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: a friend whose provider refuses (planted) reads down within one tick (TickEvery, 1 s) of her session's word, her dealt and started cards return to ready in that tick, and one judgment is raised; a friend whose presence proof merely lapses reads unknown after PresenceTTL plus DetectEvery and never down, her cards stay dealt, and the judgment is raised at UnknownRaisesAfter (20 min) with the proof's age as its evidence, the table reading down only after the seat's answer; and a class test finds no code path that writes down from an expiry; all pinned by functional tests on a real Redis with a fake clock.

Target: v1.3

From: the bus-presence store cards of 2026-10-11, from the owner's direction: nova-hook is the one way in

### A seat wait survives a reconnect and a restart

The seat's wait is a client of the comms module's timers and listener (docs/SPEC-COMMS.md 5, 7, nova-tools): a push is never lost across a reconnect or a restart, because it sits in the seat's own pending list until the seat's nova-bus ack, and the drain of the next listener generation delivers it first (5.1; no cursor is stored, the pending list is the record). A reconnect of the client resumes by that drain. A store restart fences the wait as it fences every listener (7): the waiting process is refused incarnation restarted at its next call, prints store-restarted and exits, and the live seat's re-run of the line drains the push it was waiting for; nothing resumes an old generation. The sprint's own timers are the comms module's. Absorbs (de-duplicated 2026-10-12): Timers on the sprint system that wake an actor at a chosen time (sprint-timers). Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: on the bench, a push sent during a client reconnect and one sent during a server restart are each returned by the seat's wait, the first by the resumed wait and the second by the re-run after one store-restarted line, with zero pushes lost over 100 of each and no renewal by the old process after the restart, pinned by a functional test that restarts the store mid-wait.

Target: v1.3

## v1.3 C. Sprint server conversion

The umbrella of the release: the server is the one truth, everything keyed by epoch, the tick bounded and batched, every bound a setting; then each layer secured from the bottom as the gate to the v1.4 cut. Build order.

### Sprint server conversion: test plan

The server conversion's tests, written from docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md before the theme's first implementation entry, which cites this one: unit tests on the twin store; functional tests on a real Redis and Postgres, one per Lua function the server adds; an integration run of seat, member and friend against one server on the bench; the stress drags (deals of 3,000 cards, a 140-width fleet, the tick under one second, every verb under a second while busy); the server's models with their reversed witnesses, checked by TLC on a bench; and its rows in the parallel release checks, under two minutes. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: each tier above has a named test or TLC case for the server conversion, listed in docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md, red before the theme's code and green after, with the 3,000-card deal and the one-second tick recorded.

From: the owner, 2026-10-12

### Convert every client-held copy of sprint state to client/server

The first v1.4 rewrite step. Each item in the 2026-10-10 inventory where a client keeps its own copy of sprint state is converted in place so the server is the one truth and clients ask it: the friend daemon's lanes and epoch, the member loop's lane table and local recovery (one lane protocol for friends and fleet), the seat's file proof, friend messages through folders and the separate bus Redis, config split across Postgres and the store, hosts following versions, the dashboard's own snapshot, and the lander as a second truth in git. All state is keyed by epoch. A TLA+ model of the lane protocol comes first. Faults found while the point releases run are recorded here as input. Absorbs (de-duplicated 2026-10-12): Friends are told of cards and push work reliably (friend-notification-and-delivery-reliability); The system sends the width goal to idle or under-width friends (machine-sends-width-goal-to-friends); Friend delivery is a visible state (friend-delivery-state); Friend lifecycle and widths run through the system: wake, take, refill, redistribute (friend-lifecycle-automation); All coordination state in Redis, batched, driven by Go tools (coordination-state-in-redis-and-go); Decisions are made centrally; machines only execute what the queue says (central-decisions-fleet-executes). The umbrella of v1.3, not v1.4: the roadmap's own text says v1.3 is this conversion and v1.4 its stable release. Model first (the lane protocol model, then the server's). The lane half is the one lane protocol for friends and fleet: the in-progress v1.2.6 fixes friend-lanes-are-thin-clients (nova-tools) and lanes-ask-the-server-what-they-hold are its first steps, one-shot-workers (nova-tools roadmap) its rule, and the batch delivery items named here retire with it. Every tool reaches the store through redisconn. Its tests are server-test-plan. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: no client keeps a copy of sprint state (a class test finds no lane table, cached epoch or local recovery in a client), the seat, dashboard, lander and friends ask the server, and a 140-width fleet plus friends runs a day on the bench with every judgment traceable to one server record.

Why it waits: Point releases continue meanwhile; their faults are the input to this rewrite cleanup.

Target: v1.3

### Server beats and reads run off the control line; a gone caller is never run

Verbs that only read or beat must not queue behind the single line of control, and a verb whose caller is gone is dropped. What exists (cmd/nova-sprint/servelanes.go, tla/ServerLanes.tla): a beat lane and a read lane beside the line, a gone caller's ticket served and handed back with its verb never run (GoneNeverRuns). The gap is the bar and its proof under load: the bound a gone caller is dropped within is the caller's own deadline, BeatDeadline (15 s today) for a beat and the verb's deadline for the rest, and a verb off the line answers while the line is held. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: while a planted batch holds the control line for 5 s, 140 friend beats and 20 reads each answer under 100 ms at p99 on the bench; a caller that disconnects while its verb waits for the line is served gone, never run, no later than BeatDeadline (15 s) after it went, with gone counted on the SERVE line; and ServerLanes' GoneNeverRuns, BeatNeverWaitsForTheLine and ReadWaitsOnlyForReads hold with their reversed witnesses failing as declared, all pinned by a functional test on a real Redis.

From: PR #5015

### The sprint server does not grow without bound or stop answering

The server once reached a very large resident size and stopped answering verbs while the fleet stalled behind it. Memory is bounded and a watchdog restarts a wedged server. What exists: the tick watchdog of run (--tick-deadline, TickDeadline 10 s by default, stretched to three times the median of the last 20 ticks up to TickDeadlineCap; past it the stacks are printed and the tick given up; three wedged ticks in a row exit 4 for the supervisor to restart the loop). The gap: a memory ceiling the server reads, ServerMemoryCeiling (a setting, default 2 GiB, proposed), past which the server prints its heap profile and exits for the supervisor, and the measured proof of both at the load the plan names. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: under the load drag (3,000 cards, a 140-width fleet, 200 reads) for 24 hours on the bench the server's resident size, sampled every minute, stays under ServerMemoryCeiling (2 GiB) and its hour-24 value is within 10 percent of its hour-1 value, recorded with the run; a planted wedge (a tick that never returns) is given up at the tick deadline (10 s at the drag's median) with its stacks printed, and three in a row exit 4 and are restarted by the supervisor, the restarted server answering a verb within 5 s of the exit; a planted leak crossing the ceiling exits with its profile within one minute of crossing; all pinned by functional tests with a fake clock, the 24-hour number by the bench run.

Target: v1.3

### The verifier is its own system stage

A card's checks are written before the work starts. After the work, a verifier stage of the system runs them in a fresh bench, apart from the reader, and its verdict is the merge gate: the named test must fail at the card's base and pass at its head, run by the system rather than reported by the worker. This changes the card contract (the TEST line becomes a check the system runs), the lander (one red-at-base, green-at-head run per card before the batch gate) and the reader's job (it reads a change already shown to do what the card says). Absorbs (de-duplicated 2026-10-12): System gates before reads (machine-gates-before-reads); Work lint, then a system gate before a read, then gate lint (gate-stack); A review audit (a-review-audit); Readers check four things before approving a card (reader-four-checks-before-approval); A mechanical guard check as a review verb (review-guard-check-verb); Make reads cheap with CI evidence and a short mechanical PR brief (cheap-reads-ci-evidence-and-pr-brief); Mechanical pin-check read for test-only pull requests (reader-pin-check-for-test-only-prs); Re-land and wire script-card self-verification (script-verify-wired, nova-tools roadmap). Mechanical cards are proved, not read; the work lint proves the test pins the change; the system runs the card's check red at base and green at head as the merge gate; readers check comments, fragments, paths and cross-package references before approval; the last gate audits the reads themselves; a finish whose brief names a STEP carries that STEP's last line; store.MergeStep is reachable only through its verb. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: no card lands whose named test is not red at its base and green at its head in a fresh bench run by the system, and a planted green-at-base test is refused, pinned by a functional test.

Already in the code: The card lint requires the named test to be absent at the base: rule donewhen-test-name, internal/swarm/lintbase.go:198-236 and internal/swarm/lintpaths.go:174-192. The member's native gate runs failing tests at the base only to classify a failure the worker already reported as not done (cmd/nova-swarm/nativegate.go:26-42). The lander's tree gate runs the batch at its head and reads the TEST line only to time the package (internal/sprint/gate_wall.go:46-59). No step runs the named test red at base and green at head as a gate; that is the gap. The system gates before reads item, under the sprint system, holds the cards that started on it.

Why it waits: A new system stage, not a fix.

Target: v1.3

### A plan gate before code

A card above a size bound writes a plan first, and a reader reviews the plan before implementation starts. The design agreed with the owner on 2026-10-11 has two levels. Inside a card, working splits into planning, then a plan read, then implementing: the plan is committed to the card's branch as PLAN.md, and implementing is a second take on the same branch, so a one-shot child starts from the file, not from memory; a refused plan is a re-plan take. Above cards, a plan node turns a roadmap entry into cards with their dependencies (its scope, the cards, their DEPENDS lines and a read), feeds a stream, holds the cap of about 10 unadmitted drafts, and is what nova-work later imports as a node. Both levels are modelled in TLA+ with the card machine before either is built. Absorbs (de-duplicated 2026-10-12): Evaluate plan-then-execute cards and worktree-isolated subagents (worker-plan-mode-subagent-eval, nova-tools roadmap). A producer card is planned and checked before it waits; the plan node that turns a roadmap entry into cards reads nova-roadmap (cards-remember-their-repo-and-roadmap-entry). Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: a card above the plan threshold has a plan and a plan read before its first implementation attempt, pinned by a functional test that refuses an unplanned start.

Why it waits: A new system stage, not a fix.

Target: v1.3

From: the owner, 2026-10-11: a lesson from the Cockroach Labs write-up "Five months treating bugs like patients" (MOLT Sinai)

From: the owner, 2026-10-12

### The roadmap is nova-sprint's: doctor, import and defer, on correct data

The owner, 2026-10-12: the roadmap is just future work that feeds into sprints, and also a place to push (defer) work in a sprint out to a future point. Importing things from roadmaps into sprints has been a constant pain point, because the imported entries carry dependencies that no longer exist; and this is why the roadmap is a part of nova-sprint, it is all holistically the same thing. So the roadmap tool and its doctor are nova-sprint verbs, and the sprint reads the sexp directly when it cuts cards; nova-tools runs these verbs on its own ledgers until the fold. The data: the sexp is the single source (the pages are generated, never edited) and is written only through the verbs, never by hand in the normal flow. The rule every writer keeps, before every write: each mutating entry point validates the prospective whole ledger (both files, as they would be after the write) with the doctor before anything is committed, and on any finding refuses whole with the DOCTOR lines, nothing written to either file; CI is the second line, which catches a hand edit, never the first, because a bad write caught in CI is later than the writer's own refusal. The mutating entry points, every one under that rule: the nova-work roadmap verbs that exist today (add, remove, pull, done, note, which write through one Save), the sprint's defer (today cmd/nova-sprint/defer.go splices text into docs/roadmap.sexp with no decode and no doctor: that path is replaced by the validated one), defer --stream, import, generate (make roadmap in both repositories, and the page write of every verb), the edit verb if one is built, and any verb added later; a class test finds no write of either ledger file or its pages outside the one validated write path, and a mutation fixture per verb (generate and edit included) shows a rule-breaking change refused with one DOCTOR line and both files byte-identical after. The doctor also runs in CI on every change to the sexp. The verbs: roadmap doctor checks the sexp itself (every dependency, a :depends key or a DEPENDS-ON line in a card draft, names an entry that exists and is not later in release order than the dependent, with no cycle and nothing dangling; every :release is one of the four values; every v1.3 entry has its Done-when sentence; every entry with a card draft, a brief in the repository or under tmp/next-sprint-cards, passes card lint, nova-swarm lint --card --child-rules with zero rule or step findings, and its PATHS exist at the named base; no duplicate ids or titles; ROADMAP.md and FIXES.md byte-identical to what the sexp renders; every shipped entry's landing commit reachable from the named tag; a landed card commit since the last tag has an entry), one DOCTOR line per finding with its remedy, exit 1 on any, run in CI as a class test and by make roadmap in both repositories. roadmap generate writes the pages. roadmap import cuts cards from entries and is the boundary: it, nova-card generate and the sprint's add from a roadmap entry refuse an entry whose dependencies are dangling, landed but not on the base, or cyclic, and print the same DOCTOR lines. defer pushes a card out of the sprint into a roadmap entry at a named release, carrying its brief, needs, last pushed head and reason, so nothing is lost and it can be imported again; it replaces the hand-parking of dropped cards under tmp/next-sprint-cards. defer --stream <s> --release <r> defers a whole work stream in one verb, all or nothing for the two durable systems it writes (the store and the ledger file), with the one irreversible step named as such: stopping an attempt kills a process, and restoring a card's prior table state does not restart it, so the protocol is fenced prepare, commit and recovery rather than one Lua step for two systems. Prepare: the verb takes a fence (a deferring record for the stream in the store, with a token; a second defer of the stream is refused by it), runs the doctor on the prospective whole ledger and writes the new sexp to a staging file beside the real one (refused whole here, nothing stopped, if the doctor fails), then tells every working lane of the stream to stop (within one beat, as a moved card's old run is), returns its reads and redeals nothing, recording each card's last pushed head as its carry; a stop that does not confirm within the beat plus a tick leaves the fence in place, the stopped attempts recorded as stopped, and the verb exits with the fence named, nothing moved. Commit: one Lua step, under the fence token, moves every unlanded card into its deferred record (brief, needs re-pointed to the deferred ids, carry head, the stream's branch name and release) and archives the stream's control card (the branch stays in git); then the staged sexp is renamed into place and the pages regenerated; then the fence is cleared. Recovery, on the next verb or tick that finds a fence: a fence with no commit is rolled back (the cards back on the table in their prior states, with each stopped attempt recorded as stopped, never silently restarted); a fence with the commit done and the file not yet published publishes the staged file; a fence with the file published and not yet cleared is cleared. A later import --stream <s> restores the whole set with its internal dependency order intact. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: a seeded broken roadmap (a dangling dependency, a cycle, a bad release, a missing Done-when, a lint-failing draft, a stale generated page, a missing landing entry) produces one finding each and the real roadmaps produce none; importing a roadmap entry with a dependency that no longer exists is refused with the entry and the missing id named, never admitted; every mutating verb (add, remove, pull, done, note, defer, defer --stream, import, generate, edit) run against its mutation fixture with a rule-breaking change is refused with one DOCTOR line and leaves both ledger files and their pages byte-identical, and a class test finds no ledger write outside the validated path; a hand edit that breaks a rule is caught by CI with one DOCTOR line; a dropped card round-trips defer then import with brief, needs and carry head intact; a stream of N cards with chained needs and two carry heads round-trips defer then import with nothing lost and no partial state observable in between; a crash injected at each of the three points (after the stops and before the Lua step, after the Lua step and before the file is published, after the file and before the fence clears) leaves the sprint and the roadmap in the before-state or the after-state and never a mix after recovery, the before-state showing each stopped attempt recorded as stopped and not restarted, pinned by one functional test per point; and a stream with one working card and one in review defers in one verb, the worker's lane stopped within a beat, the carry head recorded, the stream gone from where, and import restoring it.

Why it waits: The owner, 2026-10-12: roadmap imports into the sprint arrive with dependencies that no longer exist; the data must be correct; whole streams must defer atomically.

Target: v1.3

### Two new alarms

An alarm when the store's latency passes its bound, and one when a test process is left running on a fleet machine. The latency bound is a setting, StoreLatencyAlarm (default 200 ms, proposed: the perf gate already holds a where read under 200 ms of wall on the in-memory store, docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md), measured as the tick's store round trip p99 over the last TickEvery window; a test process is one whose command line matches the test runner's pattern and whose age passes TestProcessAge (default 10 min, proposed) as the machine's beat reports it. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: a planted store delay of 250 ms raises the latency alarm within one tick (TickEvery, 1 s) and one of 150 ms raises none; a planted test process 11 minutes old on a bench member raises the second alarm at the next beat and one 9 minutes old raises none; each alarm is said once and cleared once when the cause ends; pinned by functional tests with a fake clock.

Why it waits: New capability.

From: a Gemini dialog the owner shared, 2026-10-10

### A TLA+ case for the false-positive fix loop

A fix passes its own layer but keeps re-failing a sentinel above it. A TLA+ case couples components to domains: a fix confined to PATHS that never meet the regression's component exhausts its attempt bound and halts. When widened PATHS intersect the component, the fix clears it nondeterministically (it may still fail), and every failure counts toward MaxAttempts: intersection is necessary, not sufficient. Properties: a reachable fix can land (liveness under fairness), and a fix that is never right halts at the bound (safety). Open question: does a merge-queue ejection count toward the card's attempt bound? It extends the attempt-bound models in tla-card-lifecycle-counters-and-waits.

Target: later

From: a Gemini dialog the owner shared, 2026-10-10

### Coordinator drift: a root brief and two metrics

Every escalation carries the root brief, with a test that holds it. Every card cites a release-scope or fixes item directly, never through its parent card, which closes scope laundering. Drift is measured three ways: the share of newly written cards that cite no item in the release-scope or fixes file (cards carry their release); the Jaccard overlap of non-trivial tokens between a card's brief and its cited scope item, warning below a ratio such as 15%; and the branching ratio, consumer cards per producer card per wave. The blind spots these close are scope laundering, semantic dilution and scope bloat.

Target: later
